reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC5575-4-1.note: RFC 5575 Section 4: "Implementations wishing to exchange flow specification rules MUST use BGP's Capability Advertisement facility to exchange the Multiprotocol Extension Capability Code (Code 1) as defined in RFC 4760 [RFC4760]." RFC 8955 Section 4 restates this obligation; the existing superseded disposition is retained. TestIPv4FlowSpecNegotiatesMultiprotocolCapability is only registration/constructed-capability evidence. The current reactor/rfc5575_capability_wire_test.go TestRFC5575OpenCapabilityMatchesTransmittedFlowFamily additionally decodes buildOpen OptionalParams produced from real parsed configuration, verifies Code-1 families, and sends through AnnounceNLRIBatch. Matching SAFI sends exactly the required MP_REACH bytes; advertising only the other FlowSpec SAFI returns ErrNoPeersAcceptedFamily and writes zero bytes. Producers session_negotiate.go buildOpen, capability.Negotiate and reactor_api_batch.go AnnounceNLRIBatch/buildBatchAnnounceUpdate were read. Distinct matched/mismatched negotiation arms are a genuine positive/negative pair. Removed only the now-false single-polarity annotation. Independent source rejudgment only; no test, mutation, build or gate was executed by this auditor. Native observed-red renewal is a separate parent step.

RFC5575-4-2.note: RFC 5575 Section 4: "The (AFI, SAFI) pair carried in the Multiprotocol Extension Capability MUST be the same as the one used to identify a particular application that uses this NLRI-type." Successor RFC 8955 Section 4 makes the pairs explicit: "The (AFI, SAFI) pair carried in the Multiprotocol Extension Capability MUST be (AFI=1, SAFI=133) for IPv4 Flow Specification and (AFI=1, SAFI=134) for VPNv4 Flow Specification." types_test.go TestFlowSpecIPv4Basic/TestFlowSpecVPNFamily pin both constants. TestRFC5575OpenCapabilityMatchesTransmittedFlowFamily now compares parsed production OPEN pairs to exact MP_REACH output for both flow and flow-vpn, retaining the VPN RD, and rejects the crossed SAFI without output. AnnounceNLRIBatch checks the negotiated batch.Family and buildBatchAnnounceUpdate passes that same AFI/SAFI to NewMPReachNLRI. Wrong wire SAFI and shared-AFI negotiation leakage both fail. Removed only the stale single-polarity marker; successor policy remains unchanged. Independent source rejudgment only; no test, mutation, build or gate was executed by this auditor. Native observed-red renewal is a separate parent step.

RFC5575-4-3.note: Forbidden: components out of strict type order (descending or repeated). TestFlowSpecComponentsAscendingOrder (positive) adds out of order and asserts wire order 1,3,5,12, red on insertion-order emission; TestFlowSpecJoinsRepeatedTypeIntoOneComponent asserts one Type 4 component; TestParseFlowSpecRefusesRepeatedComponentType require.ErrorIs ErrFlowSpecDuplicateType goes red if a repeat is accepted.

RFC5575-4-4.note: Forbidden: a present component after a component of higher type. Positive asserts strictly ascending emitted types (assert.Less) red on any inversion; TestParseFlowSpecRefusesDescendingComponentType require.ErrorIs ErrFlowSpecTypeOrder goes red if 5-before-3 is accepted, with the ascending control accepted.

RFC5575-4-8.note: Historical identity retained; RFC 5575 is superseded, not the live authority. RFC 5575 Section 4: 'Whenever the corresponding application does not require Next-Hop information, this shall be encoded as a 0-octet length Next Hop in the MP_REACH_NLRI attribute and ignored on receipt.' The live obligations are RFC 8955 Section 4: 'When advertising Flow Specifications, the Length of the Next-Hop Network Address MUST be set to 0.' and 'The Network Address of the Next-Hop field MUST be ignored.' Both tagged functions were read. internal/component/bgp/message/flowspec_wire_contract_test.go::TestFlowSpecUpdateIgnoresConfiguredNextHop drives UpdateBuilder.BuildFlowSpec and the UPDATE writer, asserts the literal zero next-hop length and unchanged NLRI bytes with each configured IPv4/IPv6 address, and rejects a decoded forwarding address. Its producer is internal/component/bgp/message/update_build_flowspec.go::buildMPReachFlowSpec, which never reads the configured NextHop. However, gopls references for BuildFlowSpec identify internal/chaos/peer/sender.go::buildFlowSpecRoute as its only non-test caller. The daemon's config-route sender instead invokes BuildPlugin at internal/component/bgp/reactor/peer_initial_sync.go::sendPluginRoutesVia, and the independent internal/component/bgp/message/update_build_plugin.go::buildMPReachPlugin asks Family.NeedsNextHop before encoding the length. The API batch and queued RIB writers have their own family-dependent gates. Neither tagged function reaches these daemon advertisement producers. A configured-address regression in buildMPReachPlugin therefore leaves the tagged encoding assertion unchanged; this is a source-backed discrimination gap, not an executed mutation result or a present encoding defect. internal/component/bgp/plugins/rib/rib_flowspec_validation_test.go::TestRFC8955NextHopIgnoredForFlowSpec does prove the receipt clause: handleReceivedStructured receives nil, self-address and non-address next-hop bytes; each generation must remain eligible, have exactly one real candidate, and preserve the single selected rule and exact action bytes. The nil case is the conforming control; nonzero cases isolate ignored receipt semantics. gatherCandidatesHeld reaches gatherCandidatesLocked, candidateAdmitted and extractCandidate read rib_bestchange.go::entryNextHopAddr, and its FlowSpec branch ignores both MP and unrelated legacy NEXT_HOP. Existing receipt revert records prove this producer reach only. The whole historical row remains weak because the advertised-zero clause does not exercise the daemon's producing functions. No test or discrimination command was run for this judgment, and no tests or production were edited.

RFC5575-5.1-1.note: RFC 5575 Section 5.1: "This ordering function must be such that it must not depend on the arrival order of the flow specification's rules and must be constant in the network." RFC 8955 Section 5.1 restates arrival independence and network consistency. TestFlowSpecPrecedenceFromWire checks both comparison signs and self equality across prefix, component and received-byte cases. TestRFC5575PrecedenceIndependentOfArrival additionally parses independent copies in BOTH insertion orders, sorts through production Compare, and requires identical exact output for overlapping prefixes and differing component types. Compare reads components/bytes, not identity or arrival metadata. This is no longer a one-order test masquerading as an arrival-order negative. No new supersession exclusion was introduced. Independent source rejudgment only; no test, mutation, build or gate was executed by this auditor. Native observed-red renewal is a separate parent step.

RFC5575-7-1.note: Forbidden: non-zero bytes in the five octets before the DSCP, or the DSCP elsewhere. TestFlowSpecTrafficMarkingReservedBytesZero asserts ec[2..6]==0 and ec[7]==dscp with type 0x80/0x09; red on either. {single-polarity} marker present.

RFC5575-8-1.note: Forbidden: a VPN NLRI length that omits the RD octets. TestFlowSpecVPNUpdateCountsRouteDistinguisher asserts the emitted length octet 13 (8 RD + 5), red on 5; the negative subtracts 8 and require.Error goes red if the parser accepts it.
